# Open-source bounty contribution

**Need.** A pull request to a project you do not maintain is rejected or quietly ignored far more often for skipping the project's process than for being wrong. The contributor who files against a closed or already claimed issue, ships a diff three times larger than the fix, or never ran the project's own checks has produced work no maintainer will spend time on, however good the code is. The failure is almost never a shortage of code and almost always a refusal to work the project's rules, so writing more code makes it worse rather than better.

**Input.** An open issue or a posted bounty, the project's contribution guide and its AI-contribution policy where they exist, the target branch and its conventions, the project's own declared tests and linters, and the record of any pull request already open against the same issue.

**Core action.** Confirm the issue is open and unclaimed and stand down if it is not, work to the project's own contribution and AI-use rules rather than your own habits, make the smallest diff that resolves the stated issue and no more, run the checks the project itself declares, and disclose AI assistance wherever the project or the law requires it.

**Output.** A review-ready change that resolves the issue at the smallest scope that does, passes the project's own tests and linters, fits the target branch, and carries an AI-use disclosure where one is required, handed to the human who will submit it under their own identity. Nothing has been filed against an issue that was closed, claimed, or already answered by an open pull request.

## Activities

1. Confirm the issue is open, unassigned, and not already answered by an open pull request *(observe; verify-open)*
2. Read the contribution guide, the AI-contribution policy, and the target branch's conventions *(observe; read-rules)*
3. Claim the issue or confirm it is yours to take, and stand down where AI contributions are barred *(decide; claim)*
4. Make the smallest in-scope change that resolves the issue, with tests *(act; minimal-change)*
5. Run the project's own declared tests and linters until they pass *(act; run-checks)*
6. Hand a review-ready diff and pull request description, with AI use disclosed where required, to the human who submits it *(deliver; hand-off)*

## Outcomes

### the-change-is-acceptance-ready-by-the-projects-own-standard

The contribution meets the project's own bar for a change it will take, not the contributor's.

- The diff resolves the stated issue at the smallest scope that does, with no bundled refactor, rename, or unrelated cleanup that a reviewer would have to untangle from the fix.
- The project's own tests and linters were run and pass, so the change does not fail the project's automated gate before a human ever looks at it.
- The change targets the branch the project asks contributions to target and follows its conventions, rather than the contributor's house style.
- The pull request description states what the issue was and how the change resolves it, in the form the project's guide asks for.

### nothing-is-filed-that-the-project-will-not-take

No effort is spent on a contribution the project was never going to accept.

- Nothing is filed against an issue that was already closed, already assigned to someone else, or already answered by an open pull request, because that is checked before any code is written.
- A project that bars AI contributions is honored by not contributing to it, rather than by contributing and hoping the origin is not noticed.
- Where a bounty is raced, an existing attempt is found before the work starts, so two contributors do not each build the same fix in parallel.

### ai-assistance-is-disclosed-where-it-must-be

AI involvement is disclosed wherever the project's policy or the law requires it, and never hidden to look more acceptable.

- Where the project's policy asks contributors to declare AI assistance, the pull request declares it plainly rather than presenting the work as unaided.
- The disclosure is made to the human who submits, so the person whose identity is on the pull request is never made to assert an authorship claim they did not know was untrue.
- Where no disclosure is required, none is invented, but the contribution still holds to the same standard so it would remain welcome even if the origin were stated.

## Guidance

The scarce resource is the maintainer's attention, not your code, so fit the project's own rules and make the change small enough to review in one sitting. Volume loses; a single in-scope diff that passes their checks wins. Read the contribution guide and the AI policy before writing anything, and honor a ban on AI contributions by not contributing at all. Because bounties are raced, check for an open pull request against the issue before you start, or you will do work someone already did.

## Where this is worth adopting

- A bounty board like Algora or a labeled issue tracker where several contributors race the same task, so the first review-ready pull request wins and a claim posted five minutes late is wasted effort.
- A popular repository that auto-closes pull requests failing its CI or its contribution checklist, where a diff that skipped the project's own linters never reaches a human at all.
- A maintainer who has publicly banned AI-generated pull requests unless they are disclosed and pre-approved, so an undisclosed AI diff is not just rejected but marks the contributor as untrustworthy.
- A first-time contributor to a large project who does not know that a two hundred line refactor bundled with the fix is exactly what gets a pull request sent back, however correct the code is.
- A team member asked to close a good-first-issue quickly, who needs the change to fit the project's target branch and conventions rather than their own house style.

## Connector types

- source_control
- research
- knowledge_base

```json
}
```
